site_name: Skybox Chicago I / DigiCo CHI1, 800 E Devon Ave, Elk Grove Village IL 60007
operator: Skybox (Prologis JV); later HMC/DigiCo Infrastructure REIT
verification: Three separate gaps. (1) Rent billing commencing is not an outright statement that the building opened, was commissioned, or was delivered; the IT Brief page does not use any of those words. (2) The page gives no month: 'FY25' runs July 2024 to June 2025, so the billing start could fall in 2024 or 2025. (3) No opened page ties CHI1 to 800 E Devon Ave. REBusinessOnline (2022-05-02) says Prologis and Skybox 'have completed' a 189,000 SF speculative data center at that address with 'Leasing efforts are underway', which is an untenanted shell, not operation. TechPartner (2026-05-07) says CHI1 is 32 MW and leased to a hyperscale customer under a 15-year agreement, which shows a lease in 2026 but not a start date; the 2022 and 2026 pages are four years apart, so they do not bracket. DigiCo's own site could not be located by URL (several guesses did not resolve); the HMC Capital DigiCo page lists no individual properties in the fetched text; a DCD URL returned 403. DigiCo's FY25 results release or prospectus would likely settle both the date and the address.

year_evidence_quote: During 2003, our co-processing technology center was moved from Lake Success, NY to Kansas City, MO.
year_site_match: Mastercard's FY2003 10-K names its Kansas City, Missouri co-processing / back-up facility (one such facility). The street number 11530 does not appear on any opened page, but Exhibit 10.4 to the Q2 2003 10-Q (lease with the City of Kansas City for 'the data processing facility', dated as of April 1, 2003) has an Exhibit A legal description in Platte County that runs 'to the Westerly Right-of-Way line of Ambassador Drive' and references N.W. 115th Street, consistent with 11530 N Ambassador Dr.
verification: Stronger than the researcher's bracket. The same FY2003 10-K the researcher cited states the move outright in MD&A (Depreciation and Amortization), second 100,000-character segment of the page: the co-processing center 'was moved ... to Kansas City, MO' during 2003, and Item 1 says the back-up system is 'located at a separate facility in Kansas City, Missouri.' Corroboration: the 10-Q filed 2003-08-08 (Note 7) says 'In January 2003, MasterCard purchased a building in Kansas City, Missouri' and 'The building is a back-up data center which replaced the back-up data center in Lake Success, New York', i.e. already replaced by August 2003, which rules out early 2004. The FY2002 10-K (EDGAR index timestamp 2003-03-07) still had the back-up in Lake Success with migration expected during 2003. Caveats: (a) page_date 2004-03-04 is the EDGAR directory last-modified timestamp, which I am inferring is the filing date; the 10-K text itself shows only the 2004-02-24 share-count date. (b) Mastercard bought an existing building (T.W.A. Administrative Center subdivision per the lease exhibit), so 2003 is the year Mastercard's data center began operating there, not the year the structure was built. (c) The street number is not on any opened page; the address tie rests on the Ambassador Drive legal description. (d) Quotes were returned by the WebFetch reader as verbatim; I did not see raw page text. Basis could equally be labeled a regulator filing since the statement is in an SEC 10-K.
